why: Both are cool and hypnotic, but p07's filter opening into the full broken-beat drums at 0:21 is a real arrival, while p10's dark groove only rebuilds modestly after its bar-29 breakdown.
p06's wistful falling-bass guitar loop landing at full level at 0:10, with drumless floating breaks, pulls you in, while p09 stays a sunny, focus-music arpeggio that just fades after the 1:50 wash.
p07's moody Bbmaj7-Am7 groove crashing in after the muffled intro at 0:21 is immersive, while p08 is a game-style synth rush that sits at one level from 0:13 to the end despite its 1:06 stop-time.

Both are late-night and melancholy, but p06 has the bigger arrival (+17 dB at 0:10) and more breathing drumless interludes, while p10's dark trip-hop loop has only the small bar-29 dip and feels sketch-short.

p07 has the stronger drop after its filtered intro at 0:21 but then loops one hook section like a club track, while p06's sighing lament keeps pulling the mood deeper through its drumless breaks and the slowing, unresolved ending at 2:43.
p10's dark, muffled keys and lazy beat with the bar-29 near-silent breakdown are cool and immersive, while p09's bright C-major arpeggio and IV-I sway at 0:24 are pleasant focus music.
p08 is flat but at least drives hard once the full band hits at 0:26, while p09 stays gentle and sunny, with its bass entry at 0:24 barely lifting the loop.
p07's slightly dark groove landing hard after the muffled intro at 0:21 is the kind of immersive arrival this listener loves, while p09 is a pastel new-age arpeggio that fades without ever arriving.
p10's dark, hypnotic late-night mood breathes with its bar-29 breakdown and snare-roll rebuild, while p08 is an energetic but samey action-game cycle at the same volume after 0:26.
p06's wistful guitar lament with drumless floating moments at 0:58 and 1:46 is immersive, while p08's triumphant synth-rock loop stays at one energy level despite its 2:14 dropout.
